tldr: For a known finite chain with nonnegative stochastic transitions and full support only at the intervention-node marginal, a downstream causal channel is uniformly identified from arbitrary compatible observational fragments exactly when its endpoints are connected by co-released pairs using only vertices between them. A support-restricted, zero-lifted compiler built from protected generalized-inverse stitches covers structural zeros, unequal supports, and singular or rectangular channels; strictly positive rational twin chains certify every failed design. This turns a canonical partial-observability problem from a collection of sufficient formulas into a complete and checkable release-design criterion.
gap: Existing partial-observability and do-search methods are sound sufficient procedures in this level of generality. The closest matrix-equation paper proves the local four-node pseudoinverse sandwich, but no located source closes arbitrary nonmonotone paths or gives a matching necessity construction for every observational fragment design on a finite chain.
